about.title: about me
paragraphs: I’m an M.S. Computer Science student at UMass Amherst, focused on AI Safety, Mechanistic Interpretability, and ML Systems.

My work spans understanding how safety-relevant behaviors emerge inside language models and building efficient inference systems, including batching, KV-cache management, memory optimization, and model serving.
I’m open to full-time roles starting May 2027 across Software Engineering (SDE), ML Engineering, and AI, including ML Systems, Inference Engineering, AI Safety, and Research Engineering.

items.name: Refusal Decay
items.summary: A mechanistic interpretability study of how prefilling attacks weaken refusal in a safety-aligned LLM (CS 602, graded full marks).
highlights: Extracted the refusal direction via difference-in-means and traced its residual-stream projection per layer and token.
Ran causal interventions (cross-condition patching, additive injection) with PyTorch forward hooks.
Refusal dropped 0.92 → 0.32 at k=3, but neither intervention restored it (0/300): the late-layer signal is a readout, not the causal lever.
items.description: is a mechanistic interpretability study (CS 602, graded full marks) of how prefilling attacks weaken refusal in a safety-aligned LLM. Extracts the refusal direction via difference-in-means on a held-out set, traces its residual-stream projection per layer/token, and runs causal interventions (cross-condition patching + additive injection) via PyTorch forward hooks. Behavioral refusal drops 0.92 → 0.32 at k=3, the late-layer signal shifts monotone-by-depth, but both interventions fail to restore refusal (0/300): a clean null showing the late-layer signal is a readout, not the causal lever.

items.name: align-ops
items.stack: PyTorch · TRL (SFT/DPO/GRPO) · QLoRA · vLLM · FastAPI · Redis · Prometheus/Grafana
items.summary: An end-to-end LLM post-training and serving stack.
highlights: Took Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct through SFT, DPO, and GRPO with QLoRA (1.4% of parameters, 15.8 GB peak GPU).
Held-out accuracy 54% → 72%, format compliance 82% → 96%, and a 71% preference win-rate over the base model.
Serving: FastAPI gateway with Redis caching and async micro-batching in front of vLLM: 520 tok/s at 24 concurrent requests, 640 ms p95 time-to-first-token.
1.9× throughput (GPU utilization 52% → 84%), monitored with Prometheus + Grafana.
items.description: is an end-to-end LLM post-training and serving stack. It takes Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct through supervised fine-tuning, DPO, and GRPO with QLoRA (tuning 1.4% of parameters at 15.8 GB peak GPU), lifting held-out task accuracy 54% → 72%, format compliance 82% → 96%, and a 71% preference win-rate over the base model across 500 eval prompts. The serving layer puts a FastAPI gateway with Redis caching and async micro-batching in front of vLLM - 520 tok/s across 24 concurrent requests, 640 ms p95 time-to-first-token, and 1.9× throughput (GPU utilization 52% → 84%), instrumented with Prometheus + Grafana.

items.name: NEON Quantized GEMM
items.summary: A from-scratch study of quantized matrix-multiply kernels on Apple Silicon.
highlights: Went from a 3 GFLOP/s fp32 baseline to a 394 GFLOP/s int8 micro-kernel (132× faster, ~2.5× over compiler auto-vectorization) with ARM NEON sdot.
Added GGUF-style INT4 block quantization: 6.4× smaller weights than fp32.
Roofline analysis found and broke a memory-bandwidth ceiling (~4× less memory traffic).
Bit-exact verification against a scalar reference, plus p50/p99/p999 latency measurement.
items.description: is a from-scratch study of quantized matmul kernels on Apple Silicon: from a naive fp32 baseline at 3 GFLOP/s to a 4x4 register-blocked int8 micro-kernel at 394 GFLOP/s - a 132× speedup and ~2.5× over compiler auto-vectorization - via ARM NEON sdot intrinsics. Adds GGUF-style INT4 block quantization (6.4× smaller weights than fp32), SNR analysis showing per-channel scaling contains weight outliers per-tensor scaling can't (40 vs 19 dB), roofline analysis that diagnosed and broke a shared memory-bandwidth ceiling (~4× less memory traffic), bit-exact verification against a scalar reference, and p50/p99/p999 tail-latency methodology.

items.name: Provisioning Platform
items.stack: Go · gRPC · PostgreSQL · Redis · Prometheus · Docker
items.summary: A server-provisioning control plane in Go, with REST + gRPC over one service layer.
highlights: ~19,700 provisions/min across 2,500+ simulated servers at 300 concurrent operations.
Redis-TTL heartbeats detect silently failed servers in 19s with zero false positives.
Async workflow engine drove 5,250 operations to 100% eventual success through a 3% injected failure rate.
Idempotent workflows, three-role RBAC, a transactional audit log, and race-tested CI against real Postgres and Redis.
items.description: is a server-provisioning control plane in Go: REST + gRPC over one service layer, idempotent workflows, three-role RBAC, and a transactional audit log. Benchmarked at ~19,700 provisions/min across 2,500+ simulated servers at 300 concurrent ops; Redis-TTL heartbeat liveness (500/s sustained over gRPC) detects silently failed servers in 19s with zero false positives, and an async workflow engine (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claims, capped backoff + jitter) drove 5,250 operations to 100% eventual success through a 3% injected failure rate. CI runs go test -race against real Postgres and Redis containers.

items.name: GPU Scheduler
items.summary: A multi-tenant GPU scheduler with weighted Dominant Resource Fairness and best-fit bin-packing.
highlights: 542 jobs/min under a 500-job flood on a simulated 32-GPU fleet, keeping every tenant within ~1 GPU of its fair share.
p50 11 ms / p95 66 ms scheduling latency at ~75% utilization.
Tuned preemption by measurement: 688 preemptions down to 4 on the same workload.
Crash recovery from PostgreSQL with at-least-once requeueing, plus a Kubernetes executor mode.
items.description: is a multi-tenant compute scheduler with weighted Dominant Resource Fairness and GPU-aware best-fit bin-packing. On a simulated 32-GPU fleet it sustains 542 succeeded jobs/min under a 500-job flood while holding every backlogged tenant within ~1 GPU of its weight-ideal share, at p50 11 ms / p95 66 ms scheduling latency and ~75% utilization. Preemption was tuned by measurement (an unrestricted threshold caused 688 preemptions at p95 15 s; restricting to an urgent band cut the identical workload to 4 at p95 66 ms), and crash recovery reloads queued jobs from PostgreSQL and requeues running work (at-least-once). Includes a Kubernetes executor mode (implemented; benchmarks ran on the sim executor).

items.name: CS 690PF - Performance Engineering (SIMD + Cache Matmul)
items.stack: C++ · AVX intrinsics · OpenMP · perf · Cachegrind
items.summary: My consolidated Performance Engineering coursework (CS 690PF).
highlights: Hand-tuned matmul: loop reordering, unrolling, blocking, AVX SIMD (__m256), cache-aware tiling, and OpenMP.
Profiled with perf, perf c2c, Cachegrind, and TMA.
Reproduced Coz causal profiling, allocator false-sharing (Hoard vs ptmalloc2/jemalloc/mimalloc), and measurement-bias experiments.
items.description: is my consolidated CS 690PF (Performance Engineering) coursework: hand-tuned matmul (loop reorder/unroll/blocking, manual AVX SIMD via __m256, cache-aware tiling with hardware-tuned Kc/Mc/Nc + Mr/Nr micro-kernels, OpenMP multithreading), profiled with perf, perf c2c, Cachegrind, and TMA. Also reproduces Coz causal profiling, Hoard vs ptmalloc2/jemalloc/mimalloc false-sharing, and Mytkowicz measurement-bias experiments.

items.name: NGVI Curvature vs Variance
items.summary: A team research project (CS 651) on when natural-gradient VI beats Adam on ill-conditioned posteriors.
highlights: Compared Adam, closed-form NGVI, and EMA Diagonal-Fisher at matched compute, with mean-field and low-rank Gaussian families.
NGVI's advantage grows with curvature (+0.28 nats at κ≈180, +2.32 at κ≈2566).
Cutting gradient variance ~10× didn't help Adam: ill-conditioning, not noise, was the bottleneck.
items.description: is a CS 651 optimization research project (team) asking when natural-gradient VI actually beats Adam on ill-conditioned posteriors. Matched-compute black-box VI with mean-field + LRD Gaussian families and three optimizers (Adam / closed-form NGVI / EMA Diagonal-Fisher). NGVI's ELBO gain over Adam grows with curvature (κ≈180 → +0.28 nats; κ≈2566 → +2.32); antithetic sampling cut gradient variance ~10× but couldn't lift Adam off ill-conditioned plateaus, showing that ill-conditioning, not noise, was the binding constraint.

items.name: CCR Platform
items.stack: FastAPI · React · sentence-transformers · SQLite · Docker · HF Spaces
items.summary: A full-stack platform for CCR psychological text analysis: upload a corpus, pick a validated construct, and get item loadings and exports.
highlights: Embeds items and texts with sentence-transformers and scores them by cosine similarity.
Every run records its model version, item hash, and package versions for reproducibility.
Hardened ingestion, a DB-backed job queue with orphaned-job recovery, and 17 end-to-end tests that run in ~1s.
items.description: is a full-stack platform for CCR (Contextualized Construct Representations) psychological text analysis: upload a corpus, pick a validated construct, embed items + texts with sentence-transformers, and get per-item cosine-similarity loadings, distributions, and CSV export with a per-run reproducibility record (model version, item hash, package versions). Hardened ingestion (encoding fallback, delimiter sniffing, row/size caps), DB-backed job queue with orphaned-job recovery, and 17 end-to-end tests running in ~1s via a deterministic fake embedding backend.

items.name: AgenticSearch
items.stack: Python · FastAPI · OpenAI · Brave Search · SQLite
items.summary: A provenance-first entity discovery system: a topic query in, a ranked table of real-world entities out, with evidence for every cell.
highlights: Each cell carries its source URL, snippet, and confidence score.
Multi-stage pipeline: retrieval planning, page reranking, evidence classification, deterministic extraction with LLM fallback, and verification.
150+ automated tests and provider fallback across LLM backends.
items.description: is a provenance-first entity discovery system: takes a free-text topic query and returns a ranked table of real-world entities with per-cell evidence - source URL, snippet, and confidence score - across a multi-stage pipeline covering typed retrieval planning, page rerank, evidence-regime classification, deterministic extraction with LLM fallback, and output verification. Hardened with 150+ automated tests, provider routing/fallback across LLM backends, and a reviewer-facing trust UI.

items.name: AI Research Scout
items.stack: Cloudflare Workers · Hono · Workers AI · D1 · React 19
items.summary: A RAG research assistant on Cloudflare that answers only from the pages you give it.
highlights: Fetches each URL, strips HTML, chunks, and embeds with bge-base-en-v1.5 into D1.
Answers via cosine-similarity retrieval over what it actually read.
Streams chat over WebSockets, with history stored in Durable Objects.
items.description: is a RAG-based research assistant on Cloudflare: paste URLs, it fetches each page, strips HTML, chunks and embeds with bge-base-en-v1.5, stores everything in D1, and answers your questions via cosine similarity retrieval - using only what it actually read. Chat streams over WebSockets via AIChatAgent with history persisted in Durable Object storage.

items.name: Knowledge-Graph-Guided RAG
items.summary: A team-built knowledge-graph-guided RAG pipeline for multi-hop QA on HotpotQA (CS 685).
highlights: I led multi-view retrieval: sub-question decomposition, per-view dense retrieval, RRF fusion, cross-encoder reranking, and MMR.
Lifted supporting-fact recall +2.68% (54.53 → 57.21) over the KG²RAG baseline on 4,905 questions.
items.description: is a team-built KG-guided RAG pipeline for multi-hop QA on HotpotQA (CS 685). I led the multi-view retrieval component (query-side decomposition into sub-questions, per-view dense retrieval, and RRF fusion + cross-encoder reranking + MMR), which lifted supporting-fact recall +2.68% (54.53 → 57.21) over the KG²RAG baseline on a 4,905-question evaluation. Teammates added a 0–1 knapsack token-budget selector and KG construction/reasoning.

items.name: Spark ETL Optimization
items.summary: A performance deep-dive on the NYC taxi dataset (~1.4B records).
highlights: Cut end-to-end ETL runtime ~25% (17–19 min → 14.3 min).
Broadcast joins collapsed shuffle stages from minutes to ~0.05s.
Tail-latency ratio (P99/P50) down from 2.14× to 1.74× using AQE, skew handling, column pruning, and partitioning.
items.description: is a performance deep-dive on the NYC TLC taxi dataset (~1.4B records) that cuts end-to-end ETL runtime ~25% (17–19 min → 14.3 min) and drops the analytics P99/P50 tail-latency ratio 2.14× → 1.74×. Broadcast joins over the ~265-zone lookup collapse shuffle stages (minutes → ~0.05s); AQE, skew-join handling, schema-aware batched reads, column pruning, year/month partitioning + Snappy, and pre-computed derived fields do the rest. Documented as a repeatable optimization playbook (naive vs tuned).

items.name: TasteGraph

items.name: AutoEval
items.stack: Python · IR eval tooling · Git automation
items.summary: An agent that improves retrieval evaluation sets.
highlights: Proposes new queries and labels, and accepts only changes that improve how well the eval separates reference systems.
Guardrails against gaming the metric: schema checks, duplicate rejection, and a read-only holdout.
Accepted updates are Git-backed with report cards, so the workflow is auditable.
items.description: is a retrieval evaluation improvement agent that iteratively proposes new queries and labels, scores them against multiple reference systems, and accepts only updates that improve discriminative power on a holdout-heavy fitness objective. Anti-Goodharting guardrails - schema checks, duplicate rejection, read-only holdout protection - and Git-backed accepted updates with report cards keep the eval workflow auditable and reproducible.

items.name: Underdogs Fitness Platform

Multi-branch from day 1: a second branch was onboarded as a config change, with zero schema migration.
90%+ of payments moved through the portal, cutting the client's manual workload by 70%.
items.description: is a full-stack gym management platform I built solo end-to-end in ~1.5 months and shipped to a real client - live 3+ years and still running. Auth, membership + attendance, Stripe + admin manual-cash with a partial-payment ledger, cron-driven renewal automation, and multi-branch from day 1 (every entity scoped by branchId, JWT-claim auth). When the client opened a 2nd branch a year later, onboarded it as a config change with zero schema migration. 90%+ of payments moved through the portal; 70% cut in the client's manual workload.
